channel.title: Football's Greatest Bears News
channel.description: Original FGB-written Chicago Bears news briefs with source attribution for Football's Greatest Bears live programming.

item.title: Bears erase a 10-point deficit and score 34 straight to beat Cleveland 34-10 in their preseason opener
item.description: FGB brief: NFL.com records Chicago trailing 10-0 before scoring 10 points in the second quarter, 14 in the third and 10 in the fourth to finish a 34-10 Soldier Field win.

item.title: Tyson Bagent and five Bears reserves get major evaluation opportunities while Caleb Williams and most starters sit
item.description: FGB brief: Chicago used the Cleveland preseason opener to evaluate Bagent, Jahdae Walker, Salvon Ahmed, Austin Booker, Malik Muhammad II and Ruben Hyppolite II with most established starters held out.

item.title: Bears list three first-team left tackles as Braxton Jones, Jedrick Wills Jr. and Kiran Amegadjie remain in competition
item.description: FGB analysis: Chicago's first unofficial depth chart keeps the left-tackle race wide open, with CBS Sports identifying Jones as the probable favorite while all three remain listed first string.

item.title: Bears reaffirm Hammond as their sole stadium focus while evaluating a second Indiana site near the viable Lost Marsh property
item.description: FGB brief: Kevin Warren said Chicago is concentrating its stadium project in Hammond, with Lost Marsh deemed viable and Wolf Lake Terminal now undergoing due diligence.

item.title: Ben Johnson says the Bears are chasing historic scoring, shutouts and blowouts rather than treating a Super Bowl as enough
item.description: FGB analysis: Johnson has set an intentionally extreme standard for 2026, including surpassing Denver's 2013 scoring record and building the kind of dominance that extends beyond simply winning a championship.

item.title: Bears head to Cincinnati next week for a joint practice before their second preseason game against the Bengals
item.description: FGB brief: Yahoo Sports' training-camp schedule lists Chicago's next major checkpoint as an Aug. 20 joint practice in Cincinnati, followed by the Aug. 22 preseason matchup with the Bengals.

item.title: Sports Illustrated says Chicago's biggest 2026 challenge is making improvement outpace a difficult first-place schedule
item.description: FGB analysis: The Bears enter Ben Johnson's second season balancing questions about Caleb Williams' accuracy, pass rush, veteran replacements and offensive-line stability against a demanding schedule.
